title: Introduce TFState Coordinator and GPU Nodepool Rollback Handler
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: Private installs occasionally encountered mid-upgrade TF state contention across controller processes and racey GPU nodepool rollbacks when an upgrade fails partway through. This PR introduces a light-weight TFState Coordinator service and a GPU Rollback Handler Terraform module to make state locks explicit, enable safe coordinated upgrades, and provide a deterministic rollback path for GPU nodepools. Changes: 1) modules/tfstate-coordinator: new module that provisions a small, policy-driven locking table (DynamoDB-compatible) plus a controller deployment (k8s) that exposes a minimal REST API for acquire/release/heartbeat of logical state locks; 2) modules/gpu-nodepool-rollback: idempotent rollback module that captures nodepool configuration snapshots (labels, taints, autoscaling settings, subnet attachment) in an immutable S3 prefix and exposes a plan-only path for dry-run rollbacks; 3) installer/upgrade: wiring in the coordinator to the upgrade controller so the controller acquires a cluster-scoped lock before mutating tfstate-backed resources; 4) docs and examples: upgrade-playbook.md and example-migrations/ showing step-by-step for existing customers; 5) CI and tests: add terraform unit tests, integration harness that simulates concurrent runs and a failure injection test for GPU pool delete+recreate scenario. Backwards compatibility: the coordinator is optional; by default installer continues to use existing remote state locking (backend locks) if the coordinator is not enabled. Migration path and rollout plan included in the README. Testing performed: local terraform plan/apply against a small fixture cluster, integration pipeline run that simulates two concurrent upgrade controllers (conflict expected then resolved via coordinator), and manual verification on staging where we triggered a synthetic failure in nodepool upgrade and tested automatic rollback to snapshot. Rollout plan: feature-flag defaulted to off -> enable in staging -> bake for 3 days -> enable in early adopter private installs -> enable by default. Checklist: [x] module implemented [x] e2e tests added [x] docs and playbook [x] migration notes [x] canary rollout plan

review_thread: Diego: Can we avoid adding another datastore by relying on existing backend locks? Aisha: Backend locks are not sufficient for the installer controller because multiple controllers (operator + bootstrapper) race; coordinator makes semantics explicit and allows cross-account coordination. Priya: Confirm IAM least-privilege for the snapshot writer lambda. Aisha: tightened IAM policy in commit d4e5f6g and documented required KMS key usage. Liam: Request add a dry-run path to rollback module so SREs can preview changes. Aisha: added plan-only mode and test coverage. Diego: Approve after CI green. Priya: Approve. Comments addressed and small formatting nit fixed in a follow-up commit.
merge_commit_message: Squash: Introduce TFState Coordinator and GPU rollback modules; integrate coordinator with installer upgrade controller; add tests and docs
release_notes: Private installer: optional TFState Coordinator for coordinated upgrades; GPU Nodepool Rollback module providing snapshot-based safe rollback; upgrade-playbook and migration notes added; feature-flagged rollout; no default behavioral breaking changes
migration_steps: 1) Read docs/private-installer/migration-notes.md for feature-flag usage; 2) Deploy modules/tfstate-coordinator to shared infra (apply Terraform with coordinator_enabled=true); 3) Enable coordinator feature flag in installer config for staging; 4) Run a dry-run upgrade and validate plan-only rollback snapshots; 5) Promote to production cohorts per rollout plan; 6) Decommission old heuristics after 4 weeks
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the coordinator optional to allow gradual adoption. The snapshot writer uses customer-managed KMS keys; SREs must ensure IAM principal for the lambda has kms:Decrypt and s3:Get/Put for the snapshot bucket. We intentionally scoped snapshots to a per-tenant prefix to make restores deterministic.
